from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Refractive index defines how light slows down.",
            "We model electrons as masses on springs.",
            "Atoms have a natural vibration frequency."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Hook & Prerequisite Review", lecture_lines)
        
        # Initialize animation objects
        title = Text("Light Interaction", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(title, 'C3')
        
        ray = Line(start=np.array([-2, 0, 0]), end=np.array([2, 0, 0]), color=YELLOW)
        ray_label = Text("Ray", font_size=24, color="#FF00FF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(title))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(Create(ray))
        ray_label.next_to(ray, UP)
        self.add(ray_label)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(title.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Light induces electron cloud oscillations.",
            "Oscillating electrons emit a secondary wave.",
            "Interference causes a phase delay.",
            "This effectively slows light propagation.",
            "The result is a refractive index above one."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Microscopic Origin", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets
        atom = Circle(radius=0.3, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(atom, "C3")
        
        wave = Line(start=np.array([-2, 0, 0]), end=np.array([0, 0, 0]), color="#FFFF00", stroke_width=4)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FF00"), Create(wave))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF0000"),

        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Color Dependence: Dispersion", [
            "Light color relates to its frequency.",
            "Oscillation amplitude depends on light frequency.",
            "Resonance occurs near the natural frequency.",
            "Amplitude peaks significantly at resonance.",
            "This defines the dispersion curve."
        ])
        
        # Prism and light
        prism = Polygon(ORIGIN, RIGHT*1.5+UP*1, RIGHT*1.5+DOWN*1, color=BLUE_D, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(prism, 'C3')
        
        incident_ray = Line(LEFT*2, ORIGIN, color=WHITE)
        ray_path = VGroup(incident_ray)
        
        # Placeholder animations for the visual elements
        self.play(FadeIn(prism), Create(incident_ray))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        
        # Splitting
        red_ray = Line(prism.get_right(), prism.get_right()+RIGHT*2+UP*0.5, color=RED)
        green_ray = Line(prism.get_right(), prism.get_right()+RIGHT*2, color=GREEN)
        blue_ray = Line(prism.get_right(), prism.get_right()+RIGHT*2+DOWN*0.5, color=BLUE)
        
        self.play(Create(red_ray), Create(green_ray), Create(blue_ray))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        
        label_r = Text("Red", color=RED, font_size=20)
        label_g = Text("Green", color=GREEN, font_size=20)
        label_b = Text("Blue", color=BLUE, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(label_r, 'B5')
        self.place_at_grid(label_g, 'C5')
        self.place_at_grid(label_b, 'D5')
        self.play(FadeIn(label_r), FadeIn(label_g), FadeIn(label_b))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(ORANGE))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(PURPLE))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Visualization", [
            "Cauchy's equation describes dispersion mathematically.",
            "Light enters a prism at an angle.",
            "Colors bend based on their wavelength."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        formula = MathTex(r"n(\lambda) = A + \frac{B}{\lambda^2}", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B3', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Prism
        prism = Polygon(ORIGIN, RIGHT*1.5 + UP*2, RIGHT*3, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(prism, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(prism))
        
        # Light ray
        ray = Line(LEFT*2, RIGHT*0.5, color=WHITE)
        ray.move_to(prism.get_center() + LEFT*1.5 + UP*0.5)
        self.play(Create(ray))
        
        formula.set_color(WHITE)
        formula[0][0].set_color("#FF00FF") # refractive index 'n'
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        red_ray = Line(prism.get_center(), prism.get_center() + RIGHT*2 + UP*0.5, color=RED)
        blue_ray = Line(prism.get_center(), prism.get_center() + RIGHT*2 + DOWN*0.5, color=BLUE)
        
        self.play(Create(red_ray), Create(blue_ray))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Origin and Color Dependence of the Index of Refraction

sections.title: Hook & Prerequisite Review (0:00-0:45)
sections.content: Briefly revisit the macroscopic definition of the refractive index (n = c/v). Introduce the concept of the Lorentz Oscillator Model, viewing electrons in an atom as masses on springs connected to the nucleus.
sections.example: A plucked guitar string: atoms vibrate at a 'natural frequency' when light waves interact with them.

sections.title: The Microscopic Origin (0:45-2:00)
sections.content: Explain how an incoming electromagnetic wave induces an oscillation in the electron cloud. This oscillation generates a secondary wave. The interference between the incident wave and the secondary wave results in a phase delay, manifesting as a slower propagation velocity (n > 1).
sections.example: Visualize a crowd (electrons) reacting to a runner (light wave). The crowd's delay in parting creates a 'slowed down' effect for the runner's path.

sections.title: Color Dependence: Dispersion (2:00-3:30)
sections.content: Connect the frequency of the light wave (color) to the oscillator model. When light frequency approaches the natural frequency of the atom, the oscillation amplitude increases significantly. Use a graph showing n(ω) vs. ω to demonstrate the resonance effect.
sections.example: A swing being pushed: if you push at the natural frequency (resonance), the amplitude is huge; if not, the response is weaker.

sections.title: Mathematical Visualization & Conclusion (3:30-5:00)
sections.content: Present the Cauchy dispersion equation n(λ) = A + B/λ². Use an animation where a white light beam enters a prism; the screen shows how different wavelengths (colors) follow different paths due to varying refractive indices.
sections.example: A 'Rainbow Prism' simulation showing blue light (shorter wavelength, higher n) bending more sharply than red light (longer wavelength, lower n).
